@mel_k I haven’t seen your leg, so this is general advice, not a diagnosis. The rapid jump in kilometres, morning stiffness and focal soreness 3–4 cm above the heel can fit a mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy; a thickened/lumpy area can occur with that and doesn’t automatically mean a tear.

Don’t just push through the current plan, but total rest usually isn’t needed either. Cut back the running substantially, especially hills and faster work, and use cycling/swimming if helpful. Keep any running at a level that doesn’t worsen things later that day or the next morning.

For loading, heel drops aren’t wrong, but heavy, slow calf strengthening generally has better evidence than doing heel drops alone. Start at a tolerable level—often slow raises on flat ground, double-leg if needed—and gradually add resistance as symptoms allow. Straight- and bent-knee raises cover the calf well; every second day is a common starting rhythm. On more irritable days, use gentler isometric calf holds instead (for example, several 30–45 second holds). Don’t force a deep stretch off a step.

Pain guide: up to about 3/10 during loading can be acceptable if it isn’t escalating and is back to baseline by the next morning. More morning stiffness, increasing swelling, or limping afterwards means the previous dose was too much, so reduce it.

I’d avoid aggressive “stretch until it burns” work. Cortisone in or around the Achilles also isn’t a good first-line fix because of potential tendon weakening; it doesn’t address the load issue.

If it isn’t clearly settling after 3–4 weeks of sensible load modification, see any sports physio near Bayswater for an assessment and an individual progression.

Stop running and the calf work and get checked urgently that day—GP or ED—if there’s a sudden pop, a sensation of being kicked in the back of the leg, or you suddenly can’t push off. Those can indicate a rupture.

One general medication note: fluoroquinolone antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin have been linked with tendon injury. New tendon pain while taking one warrants prompt advice from your GP/prescriber, not pushing through.
